reasons: Entry-hour confinement: by_hour_utc_entry shows the strategy only opens positions in 2 of 24 hours (01 and 23 UTC), with breadth_by_hour_utc_entry = 2/2. The rule acts in under 10% of the day with no stated reason why that window should persist, which is 'behaviour confined to one part of the day' as the axis defines it. The wide spread in by_hour_utc (13/24 positive) is the expiry/settlement calendar per the seasonality_caveat, not evidence the strategy acts broadly.

Very few completed outcomes: outcomes.completed = 20 against trade_count = 167 and sessions_with_exposure = 165 out of 960. A rule that completes 20 trades across a 32-month sample is a rule that fires a few times; the monthly breadth (23/32 positive) is computed off a very thin per-cell base and cannot be read as broad-based support.

Weekday P&L is dominated by one day: Sunday contributes ~64.2k of the ~74.4k total (≈86%) while Mon/Wed/Sat are negative. Combined with the 2-hour entry window this reads as a narrow calendar niche rather than a distributed edge.
auditors.confidence_note: No out-of-sample evidence exists (validation NOT RUN), and per-cell counts behind the monthly/weekday breadth are tiny, so I cannot tell whether the 23/32 monthly figure reflects real breadth or noise on ~20 completed trades.
